card.what: Forestay chainplate: a stainless flat bar set edge-on along the stem's leading edge, through-bolted side to side, its top a tang above the deck the forestay's toggle pins through
card.boats: J/22 hero (build_j22_hero.stem_fitting, along the hero's own stem line); Catalina 22 (build_fleet c22_hardware, the generic 70 degree stem)
card.distance: arm's reach from the foredeck; the dock camera passes the bow
card.before: kit Stemhead from bk_parts.stemhead (Oct 2026): a flat deck plate with a sail-shaped tang and two pins; the hero drew a 12 x 9 cm stainless box on the foredeck 7 cm aft of the stem

references.use: the look and layout: TX 7295 EC's bow on its lift from the dock off the starboard bow (forestay chainplate edge-on down the stem, toggle on its tang, jib tack bail just aft on the foredeck)
references.url: Bean's lesson photo IMG_9224 (Oct 4 2026, project files sailing-sim-ref/j22-lessons; shows people elsewhere in the frame, so never committed)
https://rigrite.com/Spars/A_spec_classes/H_J22_mast.php (J/22 stemhead RR 79-J22 for a 3/8 in pin)

sizes.name: Bar thickness
sizes.source: GUESS: the hero's forestay toggle cheeks straddle 6.4 mm

features.text: Flat bar edge-on along the stem's leading edge, standing proud of it
Tang above the deck at the stem's top with one round hole for the forestay toggle's pin
Through-bolts side to side down the stem: dome heads one side, acorn nuts the other

budget.note: hero is a Nanite part; build_kit makes the light copy at a quarter of the triangles
